clinician.trajectory_summary: A 30-year-old male presented with hemoptysis (50-100 ml bloody sputum) accompanied by paroxysmal chest distress, shortness of breath, and palpitation. Initial evaluation showed unremarkable physical examination, mild infection on pulmonary CT (with normal recheck CT), and normal echocardiography and abdominal ultrasound. He was initially treated as pneumonia with hemostatic therapy and antibiotics with symptom relief and discharged.
